chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others besides them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
regarding this verse: 'Allah obliterates what He wills and establishes [what He wills]'
then he said: 'And is anything obliterated except that which had been established? And is anything established except that which had not yet occurred?'

key_terms.الْبَدَاء: Al-Bada' — the Islamic theological doctrine of divine modification of decree; God's ability to alter previously determined outcomes based on new conditions (e.g., prayer, repentance, deeds)
key_terms.يَمْحُوا: To obliterate/erase — used for God's capacity to remove previously decreed outcomes
key_terms.يُثْبِتُ: To establish/confirm — used for God's capacity to confirm and actualize decrees

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the Quranic verse on God obliterating and establishing decrees (al-Bada')?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a philosophical commentary on Quran 13:39, which describes God's power to erase and affirm decrees. The Imam's rhetorical questions illuminate the doctrine of al-Bada' (divine modification of decree): obliteration logically presupposes prior establishment, and establishment logically presupposes prior non-existence. This teaching was central to the early Shia community's understanding of divine will and the Imams' unique insight into the Preserved Tablet, distinguishing conditional from absolute divine decrees.
